plan: dispatch://INFRA-821/artifact/plan-md (version 1). Six text edits, this pull request's own packages/pi-legion changelog fragment, and six acceptance proofs each with a surface, a command and a negative control.

implement: legion-worker: the phase contract this change runs under - the handoff file, the push with the skip-checks trailer for a handoff-only push, the pull request body's proof rules, and the no-deferrals rule that puts the INFRA-629 tense fix in this pull request rather than a later one.

asd-ste100: the whole product is prose that agents parse with no human present (the root AGENTS.md bullet, a workflow header, two docs/solutions rules, one shipped skill reference), which is exactly the text class this skill governs.
ce-simplify-code: the implementer's once-per-pull-request simplify pass; this change edits no code, so the pass records that no code path changed rather than being skipped silently.
test: legion-worker: the tester's handoff and proof schema, and the rule that evidence names only what was run - needed here because three of the six edits (docs/solutions, the workflow header) are covered by no CI job and must be proven by grep alone.
review: legion-worker: the merge gate order, the review-thread rules, and the reviewer's own prose-fix exception, which matters on a pull request whose whole diff is prose.

thermonuclear-deep-review: the reviewer's correctness pair and its attack on the pull request body's claims - the body here carries quoted command output (the .changie.yaml format, the changie run) that must be checked rather than believed.

thermonuclear-code-quality: the reviewer's maintainability pair; its question for this diff is whether the rewritten bullet and the two learning rules stay consistent with each other and with main's own fragment names.

findings.finding: F1: sjawhar/legion#2474 (legion/INFRA-632, OPEN) removes the AGENTS.md bullet and re-adds it one sentence per line with the stale text intact, and adds scripts/semantic-line-breaks.ts plus a head note. The two changes touch the same lines, and the spec cites the bullet by line number.
findings.answer: The plan cites the bullet by its title everywhere, keeps main's one-line shape (the script is not on main today), names #2474 and its branch, and tells the implementer to re-apply the corrected content one sentence per line and run bun scripts/semantic-line-breaks.ts AGENTS.md if a forward merge brings that layout in. The architect is told so #2474's tree hears it.

findings.finding: F2: dispatch://INFRA-472, treated as the rule-setting authority, was dropped by a human (changes requested on v4: 'This is not a priority. Drop this') and specifies the opposite tooling - the seven .changie.yaml files dropping the required Issue field.
findings.answer: The plan cites the controller's rule (dispatch://INFRA-590/comment/23eaa6c1-b476-4192-b5e5-f467c9ebdea8, 2026-10-28T10:06:58Z) as the only authority, states that it documents main as it is (Issue required, value pr<number>), says INFRA-472's dropped proposal is not pursued so a reviewer who finds it does not send the work back, and restates on its own authority the two rules it needed: no existing file is renamed, and only instructions are corrected. Whether .changie.yaml should stop requiring Issue is named as a person's product choice, not asked here.

findings.finding: F3: of the three docs/solutions files the spec names, one (...-LEGION-247.md:16,28,33) is already correct - it writes the glob *.yaml with no key and no slug - and another (...-pr2233.md:22) carries the stale form inside a remedy, so correcting it needs a replacement remedy, not a deletion.
findings.answer: The plan says LEGION-247 needs no edit and why, so the implementer invents none and the tester does not read the Change bullet as unmet; it is also recorded as a spec departure. The pr2233 remedy becomes 'write each fragment by hand as pr<number>-<slug>.yaml, or run changie new at least a second apart', and the AGENTS.md bullet keeps that hand-written form, so the remedy points at a name AGENTS.md still describes. The form is main's own (packages/envoy/.changes/unreleased/pr2377-rewatch-resumes.yaml).

findings.finding: F4: the second Change bullet names no file. The sweep finds one more instruction (.github/workflows/changelog-fold.yaml:3-4, which acceptance criterion 1's paths cannot see), one evidence clause this change falsifies (...-INFRA-629.md:38), and a set of test fixtures and evidence paragraphs that must be left alone.
findings.answer: changelog-fold.yaml is edit 2 and is added to the A1 grep paths; the INFRA-629 tense fix is edit 5. The plan states that the INFRA-1-*.yaml fixtures in the three test scripts, the seven .changie.yaml headers, the four package READMEs, release-push.sh's refusals and the ...-pr2324.md evidence line are deliberately left, each with the reason, so the reviewer opens no finding on them.

findings.finding: F5: five things the rewritten bullet must state that the issue does not settle - when the fragment is written relative to opening the pull request, the same-second collision now that the name has no slug, whether Issue takes pr123 or 123, whether hand-written fragments survive and under what name, and which packages take a fragment.
findings.answer: All five are written into the bullet's content in the plan: open the pull request first and add the fragment in a later commit; run changie new at least a second apart and count, or write pr<number>-<slug>.yaml by hand; Issue takes pr<number> (fragmentFileFormat puts {{.Custom.Issue}} first and main's files read pr2371-...); the hand-written form stays and is named; and the fragment is owed by each changed package that has a .changie.yaml - the seven CHANGELOG_PACKAGES names - not by 'each package it changes'.

findings.finding: F6: acceptance criterion 1's paths miss the workflow header and its second half names no command; criterion 3 needs a real write because changie new --dry-run prints content and not a path; criterion 4 must not be widened (LEGION-1234 in packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/reclaim_doc_test.go:55 is a false red); and every criterion is negative, so nothing proves the new text is present.
findings.answer: A1 widens the paths to AGENTS.md packages/ docs/ skills/ .github/ and adds the lowercase slug pattern, with the pi-uu-grep caveat that a pattern starting with a dash is written [-][-]... and that a clean grep exits 1. A3 is satisfied by this pull request's own pi-legion fragment, with a scratch negative control under TMPDIR using --custom Issue=INFRA-821. A4 keeps the skills/ scope and names the two false reds. A5 (the staged plugin) and A6 (the new text present, four greps with their base controls) are added as criteria.

findings.finding: F7: this change earns a packages/pi-legion changelog fragment - skills/legion-retro/ is a --patch-path of pi-legion's release recipe (release.yaml:125-128) and release-bump.sh:81-83 bumps the patch version for any commit touching one - and that fragment can only be written after the pull request number exists.
findings.answer: Edit 7 in the plan: one fragment in packages/pi-legion, kind Fixed, written with the documented command after the pull request is open, in its own commit, and that run is A3's proof. The work order spells the ordering out. The plan states why packages/claude-envoy gets none: this pull request changes no file of that package.

findings.finding: F8: packages/claude-envoy/legion/skills/legion-retro/references/learnings.md is a byte-identical built copy; a pull request never commits dist/ or legion/, and CI cannot catch a stale copy because the job rebuilds and overwrites it.
findings.answer: The plan forbids touching packages/claude-envoy/legion/**, states the cost (between the merge and the rebuild workflow's push, main's committed plugin still teaches the old name - one build plus a runner queue), and requires the pull request body to say it with the reason so the reviewer does not read it as an incomplete change. A4's skills/ scope keeps the built copy out of the criterion.

findings.finding: F9: no ci.yaml change filter names docs/solutions/**, so three of the six edits are covered by no job; skills/** and AGENTS.md are what select pi_legion, docs, contracts and claude_envoy.
findings.answer: The plan names the selected jobs with their filter lines and says plainly that edits 3, 4 and 5 are proven by grep alone and by no job, so the tester's evidence claims no run that covers them.

findings.finding: F10: acceptance names no production-like surface, while the product is text three different consumers load (the repository checkout, the pi-legion plugin, the claude-envoy plugin).
findings.answer: A5 is the plugin surface: scripts/pi-plugin-prepack.sh --stage-skills @sjawhar/pi-legion into a fresh TMPDIR directory, then grep the staged learnings.md - measured working at the base, where it prints the stale line 24. The plan says the production check reads main's own tree and must not expect the claude-envoy copy at the merge commit.

findings.finding: F11: three claims in the spec the record does not support - the INFRA-750 attribution is false (it is 'Envoy bus tests on main pass every run'), the two 'cost INFRA-550 a round' claims trace only to the controller's report, and 'both put a Dispatch key into the public repository' is true of <LEGION_ISSUE> but not of the exempt LEGION-123 example.
findings.answer: The plan cites main's own learning files and the controller's rule instead of INFRA-750 (recorded as a spec departure), leaves the INFRA-550 round costs out of the plan and the pull request body as motivation only, and states the real defect precisely: <LEGION_ISSUE> expands to the deployment's own key (INFRA-821) in a public file name, while AGENTS.md's public-repository rule exempts Legion's own LEGION-<n> keys.

findings.finding: F12: the implementer is about to edit two learning documents written by other retros, which skills/legion-retro/references/learnings.md:6-10 forbids ('Never edit a document you did not write this retro').
findings.answer: The plan states that the rule binds the retro step and its reason is concurrent retros editing the same lines; this issue's Change bullet names those files, each edit stays inside the one stale sentence, and no superseding document is written.

outcome.scope: One file leaves the edit list (...-LEGION-247.md, already correct) and two join it (.github/workflows/changelog-fold.yaml, docs/solutions/best-practices/...-INFRA-629.md).

specDepartures.plan: A1 runs both patterns, plus the lowercase slug variant that ...-pr2233.md uses, over AGENTS.md packages/ docs/ skills/ .github/, and records the base run as its negative control.
